Matted nodes are not the normal finding; a normal node is round or ovoid, smooth, mobile and non-tender.
Smooth, mobile and non-tender
Correct. A normal lymph node is round or ovoid, smooth, mobile and non-tender.

B.io: e — Clinical skills for a complete and focused skin examination
B.q: A patient has bluish discoloration of the fingers and toes with a normal oxygen level. What does peripheral cyanosis usually reflect?
opts: Excess melanin production in the extremities
Increased pigmentation is a separate color change; peripheral cyanosis is usually due to inadequate circulation.
Chronic exposure to cold water
Cold water is not the usual explanation; peripheral cyanosis is usually due to inadequate circulation.
Inadequate circulation
Correct — peripheral cyanosis is a perfusion problem, which is why it spares the central mucous membranes.
Inadequate oxygenation in the lungs
Inadequate oxygenation in the lungs causes central cyanosis; peripheral cyanosis is usually due to inadequate circulation.

B.io: e — Clinical skills for a complete and focused skin examination
B.q: A patient has central cyanosis. What is the usual explanation?
opts: Increased pigmentation of the skin
Pigment change is a separate category of color abnormality.
Deposition of bilirubin in the skin
That describes jaundice rather than cyanosis; central cyanosis is often due to inadequate oxygenation in the lungs.
Inadequate oxygenation in the lungs
Correct — central cyanosis points to a pulmonary problem rather than a circulatory one.
Inadequate circulation to the extremities
Inadequate circulation produces peripheral cyanosis; central cyanosis is usually due to inadequate oxygenation in the lungs.

B.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
B.q: Which statement about otoscopic findings in hearing loss is correct?
opts: Both are usually visible
The inner ear and cochlear nerve cannot be seen with an otoscope.
Conductive loss is always visible with no exception
Otosclerosis is the exception: a conductive loss in which the abnormality is usually not visible on otoscopy.
Conductive loss is usually visible, except in otosclerosis
Correct. In conductive loss the abnormality is usually visible, except in otosclerosis, while the sensorineural problem is not visible.
Sensorineural loss is usually visible; conductive loss is not
Reversed — the sensorineural problem lies beyond anything the otoscope can reach.

B.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
B.q: When must the lid never be everted?
opts: If a foreign body has already been seen
Eversion is the way to search thoroughly for a foreign body; it is forbidden only when globe rupture is suspected.
If rupture of the globe is suspected
Correct — the lid is never inverted or everted when rupture of the globe is suspected.
If the patient has conjunctivitis
Conjunctivitis is not a contraindication; the lid is never everted when rupture of the globe is suspected.
If the patient wears contact lenses
Contact lens wear is not a contraindication; the lid is never everted when rupture of the globe is suspected.
B.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 42

B.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
B.q: Scaliness of the eyebrows suggests what?
opts: Hypothyroidism
Hypothyroidism causes lateral sparseness of the eyebrows; scaliness suggests seborrheic dermatitis.
Contact dermatitis
Contact dermatitis is not the eyebrow association; scaliness of the eyebrows suggests seborrheic dermatitis.
Psoriasis
Psoriasis is not the eyebrow association; scaliness of the eyebrows suggests seborrheic dermatitis.
Seborrheic dermatitis
Correct — scaliness of the eyebrows is the eyebrow finding associated with seborrheic dermatitis.
B.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 27

B.io: d — Physical examination findings of abnormal conditions of skin, hair and nails
B.q: A nail whose proximal portion is white and whose distal portion is dark is described as what?
opts: Mee's lines
Mee's lines are transverse lines across the nail; a white proximal and dark distal nail is Terry's nails.
Beau's lines
Beau's lines are transverse depressions rather than a color change.
Splinter hemorrhages
Splinter hemorrhages come from the distal capillary loop; a white proximal, dark distal nail is Terry's nails.
Terry's nails
Correct — the proximal white and distal dark pattern defines the finding.

B.io: d — Physical examination findings of abnormal conditions of skin, hair and nails
B.q: A reddish-purple, non-blanching macule measuring two millimeters is called what?
opts: An ecchymosis
An ecchymosis is larger than one centimeter; a two-millimeter non-blanching macule is a petechia.
A cherry angioma
A cherry angioma is dome-shaped and may blanch; a flat two-millimeter non-blanching macule is a petechia.
A petechia
Correct — petechiae are reddish-purple, non-blanching macules under three millimeters.
Purpura
Purpura measures three millimeters to one centimeter; a two-millimeter non-blanching macule is a petechia.

B.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
B.q: A patient's own voice is UNUSUALLY LOUD. Which kind of hearing loss does that suggest?
opts: Neither — loud voice indicates a psychiatric cause
A loud voice is a feature of sensorineural loss, where hearing is difficult; it does not indicate a psychiatric cause.
Sensorineural
Correct. In sensorineural loss the voice may be loud because hearing is difficult, including hearing one's own voice.
Conductive — the middle ear amplifies the patient's own voice
In conductive loss the voice stays SOFT, because the inner ear and cochlear nerve are intact and bone conduction carries the patient's own voice perfectly well.
Either — voice volume does not distinguish them
It does distinguish them, and it costs nothing to notice while taking the history.

B.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
B.q: Which bacteria are common causes of otitis media?
opts: Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae
Correct. Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae are the common bacterial causes of the purulent effusion of otitis media.
Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus
These are not the common otitis media bacteria, which are Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae.
Aspergillus niger and Candida albicans
Fungi are not the usual cause; the common bacteria of otitis media are Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae.
Streptococcus pyogenes and Moraxella lacunata
These are not the common otitis media bacteria; those are Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae.

B.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
B.q: Which pupil finding is abnormal?
opts: Any pupil under 4 mm
A pupil under 4 mm is not abnormal by itself; a size difference greater than 1 mm or a poorly reactive pupil is.
Any pupil that constricts to light
Constricting to direct light is the normal direct reflex; a poorly reactive pupil is what is abnormal.
Equal pupils that both react briskly
Equal, briskly reacting pupils are normal; a size difference over 1 mm or a poorly reactive pupil is abnormal.
A difference in size greater than 1 mm
Correct — a size difference greater than 1 mm is abnormal, as is a pupil that reacts poorly to direct light.
B.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 71

B.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
B.q: Which four dimensions assess any eye complaint?
opts: Onset, duration, severity and radiation
Radiation is not one of them; the frame is time course, precipitating factors, what helps or worsens it, and vision loss.
Location, quality, quantity and timing
Quality and quantity are not in it; the frame is time course, precipitating factors, palliative or exacerbating variables, and visual deficits.
Fever, discharge, photophobia and itch
Those are symptoms and findings, not the frame; eye complaints are assessed by time course, precipitating factors, modifiers and vision loss.
Time course, precipitating factors, palliative or exacerbating variables, and vision loss or visual deficits
Correct — every eye complaint is assessed by time course, precipitating factors, palliative or exacerbating variables and vision loss.
B.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 7

B.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
B.q: Why does moving the light to the affected eye cause BOTH pupils to dilate in an afferent defect?
opts: The ciliary ganglion has degenerated
Ciliary ganglion degeneration causes Adie's tonic pupil; the swinging light dilation comes from reduced afferent input.
The afferent stimulus on that side is reduced
Correct — the reduced afferent stimulus reduces the efferent signals to both pupils, so a net dilation occurs.
The affected pupil is pharmacologically blocked
Pharmacologic sphincter block is a cause of a dilated pupil, but the swinging light dilation comes from reduced afferent input.
The oculomotor nerve is compressed on that side
Oculomotor compression causes a fixed dilated pupil; the swinging light dilation comes from reduced afferent input from the optic nerve.
B.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 77

B.io: e — Clinical skills for a complete and focused skin examination
B.q: You press a piece of clear glass against a red lesion and the color fades. What does this indicate?
opts: Vascular engorgement
Correct. In diascopy, blood that can be pressed out of vessels blanches; blood outside vessels cannot.
Hemorrhage into the skin
Hemorrhage is indicated when the color does not fade under pressure.
Increased melanin pigmentation
Diascopy separates vascular engorgement from hemorrhage; color that fades under pressure means vascular engorgement.
Deposition of bilirubin in the skin
Jaundice does not blanch and is not what diascopy tests for.

B.io: d — Physical examination findings of abnormal conditions of skin, hair and nails
B.q: Hair loss caused by an urge to pull out one's own hair is called what?
opts: Alopecia areata
Alopecia areata is an inflammatory disease of hair follicles associated with autoimmune disorders.
Androgenic alopecia
Androgenic alopecia is male pattern baldness; hair loss from an urge to pull out hair is trichotillomania.
Hirsutism
Hirsutism is increased hair growth in women; hair loss from an urge to pull out hair is trichotillomania.
Trichotillomania
Correct — patches may be single or multiple and range from a few square centimeters to the entire scalp.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: A tympanic membrane perforation that does NOT extend to the margin is called what?
opts: Attic
Attic is not one of the two positions; perforations are central if they spare the margin and marginal if they involve it.
Traumatic
Trauma describes a cause, not a position; perforations are classed as central or marginal by whether they reach the margin.
Central
Correct. The classification is simply by whether the margin is involved, and a marginal perforation is the one that does involve it.
Marginal
Marginal perforations are the ones that DO involve the margin.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: HORIZONTAL diplopia — images side by side — points to a palsy of which cranial nerves?
opts: Third or fourth
Third or fourth nerve palsy gives VERTICAL diplopia, images on top of each other; horizontal points to III or VI.
Fourth or sixth
The fourth nerve belongs to the vertical pattern; horizontal diplopia points to a palsy of cranial nerve III or VI.
Second or seventh
Neither supplies the extraocular muscles, which are served by III, IV and VI; horizontal diplopia points to III or VI.
Third or sixth
Correct — horizontal diplopia, with images side by side, points to a palsy of cranial nerve III or VI.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 18

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: If a visual deficit is NOT corrected by pinhole testing, what should be considered?
opts: Blepharitis
Blepharitis is a lid inflammation, not a cause to consider; uncorrected loss suggests cataract, optic nerve or retinal disease.
Cataract, optic nerve disease, or retinal disease
Correct — if the pinhole does not correct the deficit, consider cataracts, optic nerve disease or retinal disease.
Simple myopia or astigmatism
Myopia and astigmatism are refractive errors, which the pinhole corrects; uncorrected loss suggests cataract, nerve or retinal disease.
Dry eye
Dry eye is not among the causes to consider; uncorrected loss suggests cataract, optic nerve disease or retinal disease.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 52

C.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
C.q: A bulla ruptures and leaves a moist area that does not bleed. How should this be described?
opts: An ulcer
An ulcer is a deeper loss that may bleed and scar; a moist, non-bleeding area after a bulla ruptures is an erosion.
A fissure
A fissure is a linear crack rather than a broad denuded area.
An excoriation
An excoriation is an abrasion or scratch mark; a moist, non-bleeding area after a bulla ruptures is an erosion.
An erosion
Correct — the moist, non-bleeding surface indicates the dermis has not been breached.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: Lateral sparseness of the eyebrows suggests what?
opts: Hyperthyroidism
Hyperthyroidism is linked to lid lag, not eyebrow loss; lateral eyebrow sparseness suggests hypothyroidism.
Seborrheic dermatitis
Seborrheic dermatitis causes scaliness of the eyebrows; lateral sparseness suggests hypothyroidism.
Iron deficiency
Iron deficiency is not an eyebrow association; lateral sparseness of the eyebrows suggests hypothyroidism.
Hypothyroidism
Correct — lateral sparseness of the eyebrows is the eyebrow finding associated with hypothyroidism.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 27

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: Endemic goiter is associated with what?
opts: Thyroid-stimulating antibodies
Thyroid-stimulating antibodies are not the association; endemic goiter is associated with iodine deficiency.
Previous radiation exposure
Radiation exposure raises thyroid cancer risk; endemic goiter is attributed to dietary iodine deficiency.
Iodine deficiency
Correct. Endemic means it clusters geographically, and the reason is dietary iodine.
Autoimmune destruction of the gland
Autoimmune destruction is not the association; endemic goiter is associated with iodine deficiency.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: Besides diabetes and hypertension, which systemic disease is a relevant part of the ocular history?
opts: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Lung disease is not among them; the relevant systemic diseases are diabetes, hypertension and human immunodeficiency virus disease.
Gastroesophageal reflux disease
Reflux disease is not among them; the relevant systemic diseases are diabetes, hypertension and human immunodeficiency virus disease.
Iron deficiency anemia
Anemia is not among them; the relevant systemic diseases are diabetes, hypertension and human immunodeficiency virus disease.
Human immunodeficiency virus disease
Correct — the relevant systemic diseases to ask about are diabetes, hypertension and human immunodeficiency virus disease.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 14

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: Injection localized JUST AROUND THE CORNEA suggests which three conditions?
opts: Keratitis, iritis, or acute glaucoma
Correct — injection just around the cornea could result from keratitis, iritis or acute glaucoma.
Conjunctivitis, blepharitis, or dry eye
Conjunctivitis gives diffuse redness maximal peripherally, not a ring around the cornea; that ring suggests keratitis, iritis or glaucoma.
Subconjunctival hemorrhage, pinguecula, or pterygium
Those are localized patches or growths of the conjunctiva; injection just around the cornea suggests keratitis, iritis or acute glaucoma.
Episcleritis, chalazion, or hordeolum
Those are nodules and lid lesions; injection just around the cornea suggests keratitis, iritis or acute glaucoma.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 46

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: After a chemical or fluid splash to the eye, what must you establish?
opts: Whether the patient was wearing contact lenses
Contact lens wear is not the essential fact here; you must establish the acidity or alkalinity of the fluid.
The manufacturer of the product
The brand is not what matters; the essential fact after a chemical exposure is its acidity or alkalinity.
The acidity or alkalinity of the fluid
Correct — after any chemical or fluid exposure, knowing whether the fluid was acidic or alkaline is essential.
The volume of fluid involved
Volume is not what must be known; you must establish whether the fluid or chemical was acidic or alkaline.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 15

C.io: d — Physical examination findings of abnormal conditions of skin, hair and nails
C.q: Scaling, sharply demarcated round plaques with central clearing describe which infection?
opts: Tinea pedis
Tinea pedis produces dry scaling or macerated fissuring of the interdigital spaces.
Tinea capitis
Tinea capitis produces round scaling patches of alopecia; round plaques with central clearing are tinea corporis.
Tinea cruris
Tinea cruris is infection of the groin; scaling round plaques with central clearing on the body are tinea corporis.
Tinea corporis
Correct — the ring with a clear center is what gives ringworm its common name.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: Which cranial nerves carry referred pain to the ear?
opts: XI and XII
Accessory and hypoglossal — motor nerves to the shoulder and tongue.
V, VII, IX and X
Correct. Four nerves supply sensation to the ear, which is exactly why disease well away from the ear can present as otalgia.
III, IV and VI
The ocular motor nerves. They have no sensory supply to the ear.
VIII alone
Cranial nerve VIII is vestibulocochlear — hearing and balance, not pain sensation.

C.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
C.q: A generalized or diffuse distribution most commonly suggests which category of disease?
opts: A fungal infection
Tinea infections are regional, confined to a specific body area.
A malignancy
Skin cancers follow a sun-exposed distribution; a generalized or diffuse distribution suggests an allergic reaction.
A pressure injury
Pressure injuries occur where pressure is applied rather than diffusely.
An allergic reaction
Correct — a process delivered through the bloodstream reaches the whole skin surface.

C.io: g — Documentation of a complete history and physical examination
C.q: What must be done if part of the examination was not performed?
opts: Leave the section blank without further comment
A blank section leaves the omission unexplained; if part of the examination was not done, the note must document why.
Obtain the finding from a classmate who examined the same patient
A note may not be written with another student, and the finding would still not be yours.
Document why it was not done — findings may never be invented
Correct — history and examination findings may never be made up; if something was not done, the note documents why.
Record the finding that would be expected if it were normal
Recording an expected finding for an untested part is making up a finding; the note must document why it was not done.
C.cite: Intro to PD II - Elwaya .pdf, Page 20

C.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
C.q: An eruption confined to a single dermatome should suggest which diagnosis?
opts: Herpes zoster
Correct — dermatomal distribution is the defining feature of zoster.
Psoriasis
Psoriasis follows an extensor distribution rather than a dermatomal one.
Intertrigo
Intertrigo follows a flexor distribution in the skin folds; an eruption confined to one dermatome suggests herpes zoster.
Tinea capitis
Tinea capitis is a regional eruption confined to the scalp; a single-dermatome eruption suggests herpes zoster.

C.io: c — Clinical reasoning in oral presentations
C.q: What should the opening statement of an oral case presentation include?
opts: The diagnosis and the proposed treatment plan
Those belong at the end; opening with them removes the reasoning the listener is meant to follow.
The complete review of systems, system by system
A presentation carries pertinent positives and negatives, not the entire review.
The laboratory and imaging results obtained so far
Results come later in the presentation, not in the opening statement.
The past medical history and the chief complaint
Correct — those two orient the listener before any detail follows.
C.cite: Intro to PD II - Elwaya .pdf, Page 9

C.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
C.q: Warts are caused by which organism?
opts: Staphylococcus aureus
This organism causes pustular infections such as impetigo and paronychia.
Human papillomavirus
Correct — verrucae are small harmless tumors of the skin, gray to flesh colored, sometimes with rough hornlike projections.
Herpes simplex virus
Herpes simplex produces grouped vesicles in a herpetiform pattern; warts are caused by human papillomavirus.
A dermatophyte fungus
Fungal infection causes tinea of the body, feet, scalp and nails; warts are caused by human papillomavirus.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: A patient's eye pain is relieved by a topical anesthetic. What does that suggest?
opts: Relief suggests a deep source; no relief suggests a surface problem
This reverses it: relief points to a surface cause such as corneal injury, and no relief points to a deeper source.
Relief confirms acute glaucoma
Acute narrow angle glaucoma causes deep pain, and pain from a deeper source is not relieved by topical anesthetic.
The response tells you nothing about depth
The response does separate depth: relief suggests a surface injury, and pain not relieved suggests a deeper source.
Relief suggests a surface problem such as a corneal injury
Correct — a corneal injury feels better with anesthetic, whereas pain that is not relieved may come from a deeper source.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 12

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: How is nasal patency tested?
opts: Occlude one nostril and ask the patient to breathe in
Correct. Each side is tested separately, because unilateral obstruction is what carries the worrying differential.
Ask the patient to blow the nose and listen for asymmetry
Blowing the nose tells you nothing about which side is obstructed. Each nostril is occluded in turn and the patient breathes in.
Hold a mirror under the nose and compare the two areas of condensation
A mirror would show condensation from both nostrils together; the test isolates one side at a time.
Transilluminate each nostril in a dark room
Transillumination assesses the sinuses; patency is tested by occluding one nostril and having the patient breathe in.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: Tinnitus WITH hearing loss and vertigo together points to which diagnosis?
opts: Ménière disease
Correct. Tinnitus with hearing loss AND vertigo together is Ménière; it is the combination that makes the diagnosis, not any one of the three.
Benign positional vertigo
Positional vertigo has no tinnitus and does not affect hearing.
Acute labyrinthitis
Vestibular neuronitis leaves hearing unaffected and produces no tinnitus.
Otitis externa
Otitis externa is a disease of the canal, which looks swollen, moist and tender; tinnitus with hearing loss and vertigo is Ménière disease.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: In which three situations should the pupils NOT be dilated?
opts: If visual acuity is reduced in either eye
Reduced acuity is not a contraindication; avoid dilation for serial neurologic exams, post-cataract elderly patients or suspected angle closure.
If serial neurologic examinations are required, in elderly patients who have had cataract surgery, and if acute angle-closure glaucoma is suspected
Correct — do not dilate when serial neurologic exams are needed, in elderly patients after cataract surgery, or if angle closure is suspected.
In any patient over sixty-five, in diabetics, and in contact lens wearers
Age alone is not the rule; it is elderly patients who have had cataract surgery, plus serial neurologic exams and suspected angle closure.
If the patient has conjunctivitis, blepharitis or dry eye
Surface conditions are not contraindications; avoid dilation for serial neurologic exams, post-cataract elderly patients and suspected angle closure.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 99

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: What does a HAZY cornea in a suspected abrasion suggest?
opts: Bacterial infection should be suspected
Correct — if the cornea is hazy in a suspected abrasion, a bacterial infection should be suspected.
The abrasion is healing normally
Haziness is not a healing sign; in a suspected abrasion a hazy cornea should raise suspicion of bacterial infection.
The fluorescein was applied incorrectly
Haziness is a finding in the cornea, not a staining error; it should raise suspicion of bacterial infection.
Raised intraocular pressure
A steamy cornea goes with acute glaucoma's pressure rise; in an abrasion, haziness suggests bacterial infection.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 120

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: A firm raised lesion at an old ear piercing site. Which description fits?
opts: Basal cell carcinoma — more common in darker-skinned individuals
Basal cell carcinoma is a malignancy, and the association runs the other way.
A keloid — scar tissue, more common in darker-skinned individuals
Correct. Keloids are commonest on the shoulders and upper chest but arise at piercing sites, which puts them on the ear.
Tophi — and there is no skin-type association
Tophi are uric acid deposits of chronic tophaceous gout, not related to piercing.
A cutaneous cyst — more common in darker-skinned individuals
Cutaneous cysts are usually epidermoid or pilar and carry no such association.

C.io: d — Physical examination findings of abnormal conditions of skin, hair and nails
C.q: Which component of the triple response of Lewis is produced by transudation of fluid?
opts: The formation of a linear wheal
Correct — fluid leaving the vessels creates the raised, edematous wheal.
The initial red line
The initial red line comes from capillary dilatation; the wheal forms from transudation of fluid.
The reflex flare with broadening erythema
The flare comes from arteriolar dilatation; transudation of fluid produces the linear wheal.
The fading of the lesion after several minutes
Fading is not one of the three components; they are a red line, a flare and a linear wheal from transudation.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: What should you do if nystagmus is seen on lateral gaze?
opts: Bring the finger back into binocular vision
Correct — bring the finger back into binocular vision; nystagmus that persists there suggests a neurologic condition.
Repeat the test with the other eye covered
Covering an eye is not the step; bring the finger back into the binocular field and see whether the nystagmus persists.
Refer immediately regardless
A few beats on lateral gaze are normal, so first bring the finger back into binocular vision and see if it persists.
Measure the intraocular pressure
Pressure has no role here; bring the finger back into binocular vision and consider neurologic disease if nystagmus persists.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 63

C.io: e — Clinical skills for a complete and focused skin examination
C.q: How should the scalp be examined?
opts: Ask the patient to wet the hair before inspection
Wetting the hair is not part of it; the hair is separated into sections so the scalp can be observed directly.
Separate the hair into sections in order to observe the scalp beneath
Correct — the hair is separated into sections so the scalp can be observed, including behind the ears and the occiput.
Inspect the hair from a distance without touching the patient
Distant inspection cannot show the scalp; the hair must be separated into sections to observe the scalp beneath.
Palpate the scalp through the hair without visual inspection
Palpation alone misses the findings; separate the hair and look for lesions, discolorations, flaking or parasites.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: What is the abnormal finding on the swinging light test?
opts: Failure of the consensual reflex with a normal direct reflex — an efferent defect
The abnormal response is afferent, from the optic nerve: the consensual reflex is intact and the pupil dilates to direct light.
Both pupils constricting more than expected
Brisk constriction of both pupils is the normal response; the abnormal one is paradoxical dilation to direct light.
The pupil failing to constrict on accommodation only
A pupil that fails only on accommodation is not the finding; the swinging light abnormality is paradoxical dilation to direct light.
Paradoxical pupil DILATION to direct light with an intact consensual reflex
Correct — an afferent optic nerve lesion, the Marcus Gunn pupil, dilates paradoxically to direct light while the consensual reflex stays intact.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 76

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: What does GENERALIZED lymphadenopathy raise?
opts: Thyroiditis and goiter
Thyroiditis and goiter are thyroid findings; generalized lymphadenopathy raises causes such as lymphoma and leukemia.
Human immunodeficiency virus
Correct. Generalized lymphadenopathy raises human immunodeficiency virus infection, Epstein-Barr virus, lymphoma, leukemia and sarcoidosis.
Dental infection and tonsillitis
Dental infection and tonsillitis cause regional node enlargement; generalized enlargement raises lymphoma or leukemia.
Otitis media and otitis externa
Otitis media and otitis externa drain to specific node groups, producing regional rather than generalized enlargement.

C.io: e — Clinical skills for a complete and focused skin examination
C.q: Which features should be inspected in the nail beds?
opts: Capillary refill time and nail bed temperature
Capillary refill and temperature are not inspected; the nail beds are checked for shape, size, color, brittleness, hemorrhages, lines, clubbing and pitting.
Length, cleanliness and evidence of biting
Length and biting are not the features; inspect shape, size, color, brittleness, hemorrhages, lines, clubbing and pitting.
Shape, size, color, brittleness, hemorrhages, lines and grooves, clubbing and pitting
Correct — eight features, each of which can point toward a systemic diagnosis.
Shape and color only, since the remainder require specialist assessment
Shape and color are only two; also inspect size, brittleness, hemorrhages, lines and grooves, clubbing and pitting.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: Why should recent dental work be asked about when a patient presents with facial pain?
opts: Dental work is a recognized cause of epistaxis
Dental work is not an epistaxis cause; those are trauma, inflammation, dry mucosa, foreign body and tumor.
Dental infection is the commonest cause of frontal sinusitis
The link is with the maxillary sinuses, not the frontal ones; recent dental work may affect the maxillary sinuses.
Dental work may affect the maxillary sinuses
Correct. The maxillary sinus floor sits directly above the upper tooth roots, so a dental procedure can present as sinus pain.
Dental anesthetic commonly causes anosmia
Anosmia is asked about separately in the nose history; it is not tied to dental anesthetic.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: What is the pattern of redness in conjunctivitis?
opts: Diffuse dilation of the conjunctival vessels
Correct — conjunctivitis shows diffuse dilation of the conjunctival vessels, with redness maximal peripherally.
Redness maximal around the cornea, sparing the periphery
Injection just around the cornea suggests keratitis, iritis or acute glaucoma; conjunctivitis is diffuse and maximal peripherally.
A single sharply demarcated red patch
A sharply demarcated red area is a subconjunctival hemorrhage; conjunctivitis shows diffuse dilation of conjunctival vessels.
A violaceous discoloration of the sclera
Conjunctivitis does not discolor the sclera; it shows diffuse dilation of the conjunctival vessels, maximal peripherally.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 45

C.io: d — Physical examination findings of abnormal conditions of skin, hair and nails
C.q: Where are the lesions of Kaposi's sarcoma typically distributed?
opts: Confined to sun-exposed areas of the face
That is the distribution of basal and squamous cell carcinoma.
Confined to a single dermatome
A dermatomal pattern belongs to herpes zoster; Kaposi's sarcoma is widely disseminated over the legs, trunk, arms, neck and head.
Confined to the skin creases and folds
Skin creases and folds are an intertriginous pattern; Kaposi's sarcoma is widely disseminated over the legs, trunk and arms.
Widely disseminated on the legs
Correct — Kaposi's sarcoma is widely disseminated on the legs, trunk, arms, neck and head.

C.io: c — Elements of the history that identify skin, hair and nail disorders
C.q: Which statement about pruritus is correct?
opts: It is a sensation that causes the desire to scratch and is not itself a diagnosis
Correct — treating pruritus as a diagnosis is the error being warned against.
It is a diagnosis in its own right when no rash is visible
Pruritus is a symptom regardless of whether a rash is present.
It always indicates an allergic cause
Pruritus has many causes besides allergy, from dry skin and aging to uremia, jaundice, lymphomas, leukemias and lice.
It is only clinically significant when it disturbs sleep
Significance is not defined by whether it wakes the patient.

C.io: c — Clinical reasoning in oral presentations
C.q: What is the test of whether an oral case presentation was a good one?
opts: It leads the listener to the same differential the presenter reached
Correct — a good oral case presentation leads the listener to the same differential the presenter formulated.
It lasts less than two minutes from start to finish
Length is not the measure of whether a presentation succeeded.
It includes every element contained in the written note
A presentation is a well-organized vignette of the patient and the clinical problem, not the written note read aloud.
It avoids all medical terminology in favor of plain language
Plain language matters with patients, not in a case presentation to a colleague.
C.cite: Intro to PD II - Elwaya .pdf, Page 9

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: What causes a PERFORATED nasal septum?
opts: Trauma, surgery or drug use
Correct. All three destroy the septal blood supply or the cartilage itself, and drug use is the one patients do not volunteer.
Allergic rhinitis and chronic sinusitis
Allergic rhinitis and chronic sinusitis inflame the mucosa without destroying the cartilage underneath it.
A foreign body lodged for several days
A foreign body causes unilateral obstruction rather than perforation; septal perforation comes from trauma, surgery or drug use.
Repeated epistaxis from Kiesselbach's plexus
Bleeding from the anterior septum does not itself perforate it.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: Which three structures are inspected and palpated before the otoscope is picked up?
opts: The parotid gland, the temporomandibular joint and the zygomatic arch
The temporomandibular joint matters for referred pain on history; the ear exam inspects and palpates the auricles, mastoid and tragus.
The preauricular, postauricular and occipital nodes
Those nodes belong to the neck lymph node examination; the ear itself is inspected and palpated at the auricle, mastoid and tragus.
The auricles, the mastoid and the tragus
Correct. Tenderness found here localizes disease before anything is put into the canal, and tragal tenderness in particular points to the canal itself.
The tympanic membrane, the ossicles and the cochlea
None of these can be inspected or palpated from outside; the first is seen only through the otoscope.

C.io: d — Physical examination findings of abnormal conditions of skin, hair and nails
C.q: A purplish-blue non-blanching macule larger than one centimeter that fades over time is called what?
opts: A petechia
A petechia is under three millimeters; a purplish-blue macule over one centimeter is an ecchymosis.
A spider angioma
A spider angioma has a central red macule with radiating arms and blanches.
An ecchymosis
Correct — the change in color over time reflects breakdown of extravasated blood.
Purpura
Purpura measures three millimeters to one centimeter; a non-blanching macule over one centimeter is an ecchymosis.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: What does the canal look like in ACUTE otitis externa?
opts: Normal, with the abnormality confined to the tympanic membrane
Otitis externa is a disease of the canal, which is precisely how it is distinguished from middle ear disease.
Swollen, narrow, moist, pale and tender, and it may be erythematous
Correct. The swelling and tenderness dominate, and the narrowing is often what makes the examination difficult.
Thickened, red and itchy
That is the CHRONIC picture. The acute canal is swollen and painful rather than thickened and itchy.
Dry, scaly and pale, with no tenderness
Tenderness defines acute otitis externa, in which the canal is swollen, narrow, moist and pale rather than dry.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: Which four elements make up the ocular history?
opts: Fever, weight loss, night sweats and rash
Those are constitutional symptoms; the ocular history asks about corrective lenses, eye problems, eye medications and eye surgery.
Family history alone
Family history is not one of the four; they are corrective lenses, eye problems, eye medications and eye surgery history.
Corrective lenses, acute or chronic eye problems, eye medications, and eye surgery history
Correct — the ocular history covers corrective lenses, acute or chronic eye problems such as glaucoma, eye medications and eye surgery.
Smoking, alcohol, occupation and hobbies
Those belong to a general social history; the ocular history asks about lenses, eye problems, eye medications and eye surgery.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 13

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: A patient speaks unusually SOFTLY despite a hearing complaint. Which loss does that point to?
opts: Sensorineural — the patient compensates by speaking quietly
The opposite: sensorineural loss tends to make the voice loud, because hearing is difficult for the patient.
Mixed loss only
A soft voice is a feature of conductive loss, where the inner ear and cochlear nerve are intact; it is not specific to mixed loss.
Presbycusis specifically
Presbycusis is sensorineural, and would make the voice loud.
Conductive — the inner ear and cochlear nerve are intact
Correct. In conductive loss the voice remains soft because the inner ear and cochlear nerve are intact, so the patient's own voice is heard normally.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: Which three features define Horner syndrome?
opts: Ptosis, mydriasis, lateral deviation, and a fixed pupil
A fixed dilated pupil with ptosis and lateral deviation is oculomotor palsy; Horner gives ptosis, miosis and anhidrosis.
Lid lag, proptosis, chemosis and diplopia
Lid lag and proptosis are hyperthyroid and Graves signs; Horner syndrome gives ptosis, miosis and anhidrosis.
A large slow pupil with reduced light reaction and slow near reaction
A large pupil with slow light and near reactions is Adie's tonic pupil; Horner syndrome gives a small pupil with ptosis.
Ptosis, miosis of the affected eye, anhidrosis of the ipsilateral face
Correct — Horner syndrome gives ptosis, miosis and ipsilateral facial anhidrosis, and the small pupil still reacts to light and near.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 88

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: Which cause of red eye has no discharge, an unaffected pupil, a clear cornea and no pain?
opts: Glaucoma
Glaucoma has severe aching pain, a steamy cloudy cornea and a dilated fixed pupil.
Subconjunctival hemorrhage
Correct — subconjunctival hemorrhage has absent pain and discharge, an unaffected pupil and vision, and a clear cornea.
Conjunctivitis
Conjunctivitis has watery, mucoid or mucopurulent discharge and mild discomfort, though its pupil and cornea are normal.
Acute iritis
Acute iritis has moderate aching pain and a pupil that may be small and irregular.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 48 (image only)

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: Which two situations can the tuning fork tests NOT distinguish?
opts: Normal hearing from bilateral sensorineural loss, and normal hearing from mixed conductive and sensorineural loss
Correct. Both tests work by comparing sides or routes, so a loss that is symmetrical or that affects both routes leaves the comparison looking normal.
Conductive from sensorineural loss
That is precisely what they DO distinguish: the tuning fork tests separate conductive from sensorineural loss.
Right-sided from left-sided loss
Right-sided from left-sided loss is exactly what the Weber test answers, by lateralization in unilateral hearing loss.
Presbycusis from noise-induced loss
Neither test names a cause such as presbycusis; what they cannot tell apart is normal hearing from bilateral sensorineural or mixed loss.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: A patient says others mumble, and that they struggle most in a noisy restaurant. Which kind of hearing loss does that pattern suggest?
opts: Sensorineural
Correct. Sensorineural loss brings trouble understanding speech, complaints that others mumble, and hearing that worsens in noisy environments.
Conductive — noise masks the residual hearing
The opposite. In conductive loss a noisy environment may actually HELP, because the background is attenuated along with everything else.
Mixed loss, which always presents this way
No pattern is specific to mixed loss; the history described points to the sensorineural component.
Neither — this is a description of tinnitus
Tinnitus is sound with no external source. This patient is describing difficulty with external sound.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: Which examination comes FIRST in the suggested order?
opts: Visual acuity
Visual acuity follows inspection and the external examination of the cornea, lens and pupils.
Direct ophthalmoscopy
Direct ophthalmoscopy comes last, among the special tests with the slit lamp and ocular pressure; inspection comes first.
Ocular pressure
Ocular pressure is a special test near the end, done only if it can be measured accurately and safely; inspection comes first.
Inspection
Correct — the suggested order begins with inspection, then the external examination, before acuity and fields.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 21

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: How is transillumination of the MAXILLARY sinus performed?
opts: Shine the light into the nostril and look at the forehead
Shining the light into the nostril tests nothing; the maxillary sinus is lit from below the medial canthus.
In a dark room, shine the light down below the inner eye corner
Correct. In a dark room the light shines down just below the inner corner of the eye, with the patient's mouth open.
In a dark room, shine the light up under the brow close to the nose
Shining the light up under the brow close to the nose is the frontal sinus technique, not the maxillary one.
In a bright room, shine the light through the cheek from the side
A dark room is required, and the light is placed below the medial canthus.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: What is interrupted in Horner syndrome?
opts: The oculomotor nerve
Oculomotor paralysis gives a dilated fixed pupil with lateral deviation; Horner syndrome is a sympathetic interruption.
The optic nerve
Optic nerve damage gives an afferent (Marcus Gunn) defect; Horner syndrome is a sympathetic interruption.
The sympathetic supply to the pupil and the levator palpebrae superioris
Correct — interrupting sympathetic supply to the pupil and levator palpebrae superioris explains both the miosis and the ptosis.
The parasympathetic supply through the ciliary ganglion
Parasympathetic loss at the ciliary ganglion produces Adie's tonic pupil; Horner syndrome is a sympathetic interruption.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 88

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: What are the fundoscopic findings in glaucomatous cupping?
opts: An enlarged cup with vessels sinking in
Correct — raised pressure in the eye enlarges the physiologic cup beyond half the disc diameter, with vessels sinking in around it.
A pink swollen disc with blurred margins
A pink swollen disc with blurred margins is papilledema from raised intracranial pressure, where the cup is not visible.
A white disc with absent vessels
A white disc without its tiny vessels is optic atrophy; glaucomatous cupping enlarges the cup beyond half the disc.
A cherry-red spot at the macula
A cherry-red macula is not a cupping finding; glaucomatous cupping enlarges the cup beyond half the disc diameter.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 103

C.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
C.q: Fine scale that is attached at the periphery and detached at the center, seen at the edge of an inflammatory lesion, is called what?
opts: Crust
A crust is dried serum, blood and cellular debris; fine scale attached at the periphery is collarette scale.
Excoriation
An excoriation is a scratch mark; fine scale attached peripherally and detached centrally is collarette scale.
Collarette scale
Correct — pityriasis rosea is the condition in which it is classically seen.
Lichenification
Lichenification is thickening with accentuated skin lines; peripherally attached, centrally detached scale is collarette scale.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: Which interpretation of an ABSENT glow on sinus transillumination is correct?
opts: Thickened mucosa or secretions, and it is diagnostic of sinusitis
Transillumination is neither sensitive nor specific, so an absent glow cannot be diagnostic of sinusitis on its own.
A normal air-filled sinus
An air-filled sinus transmits the light, so a normal sinus GLOWS.
A deviated septum
Transillumination looks at the sinuses, not the septum; an absent glow suggests thickened mucosa or secretions.
Thickened mucosa or secretions, but the test is not specific
Correct. Absence of glow suggests thickened mucosa or secretions, but transillumination is neither sensitive nor specific.

C.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
C.q: How is an atrophic scar described?
opts: Rough with accentuated skin lines
Rough skin with accentuated lines is lichenification; an atrophic scar is thin and white.
Thin and white
Correct — as opposed to a hypertrophic scar, which is thick and pink.
Thick and pink
Thick and pink describes a hypertrophic scar; an atrophic scar is thin and white.
Raised and extending beyond the wound
A raised scar extending beyond the wound is a keloid; an atrophic scar is thin and white.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: A diffusely enlarged, FIRM thyroid points to what?
opts: A multinodular goiter
A multinodular goiter is nodular rather than diffuse; firm diffuse enlargement points to Hashimoto thyroiditis.
Thyroid carcinoma
A single hard nodule would raise that, not diffuse firm enlargement.
Hashimoto thyroiditis
Correct. Firmness is the feature that separates it from Graves, where the gland is soft.
Graves disease
Graves disease gives a soft diffuse enlargement; a firm, diffusely enlarged gland points to Hashimoto thyroiditis.

C.io: d — Physical examination findings of abnormal conditions of skin, hair and nails
C.q: Partial thickness skin loss involving the epidermis, dermis or both defines which stage of pressure ulcer?
opts: Stage II
Correct — partial thickness is what distinguishes stage II from the full thickness loss of stage III.
Stage I
In stage I the skin is still intact; partial thickness skin loss of the epidermis, dermis or both is stage II.
Stage III
Stage III is full thickness loss with subcutaneous necrosis.
Stage IV
Stage IV destroys tissue, muscle and bone; partial thickness loss of the epidermis or dermis is stage II.

C.io: d — Physical examination findings of abnormal conditions of skin, hair and nails
C.q: Which term refers to a tinea infection of the groin?
opts: Tinea unguium
Tinea unguium is infection of the nails; a tinea infection of the groin is tinea cruris.
Tinea cruris
Correct — cruris denotes the groin, just as corporis denotes the body and capitis the scalp.
Tinea corporis
Tinea corporis is infection of the body; a tinea infection of the groin is tinea cruris.
Tinea capitis
Tinea capitis is infection of the scalp; a tinea infection of the groin is tinea cruris.

C.io: c — Elements of the history that identify skin, hair and nail disorders
C.q: Which set of questions forms the core of a proper dermatological history?
opts: The results of any previous biopsy, culture and blood work
Prior testing is useful background but is not the core of the history.
Where the problem first appeared, what it looked like, how it has progressed, associated symptoms, and what treatment has been tried
Correct. Those five questions cover onset, original appearance, evolution, symptoms and prior therapy.
The patient's age, occupation, marital status and insurance carrier
These are demographic details rather than the history of the skin problem itself.
Whether the lesion is a macule, papule, plaque or nodule
Morphology is determined on examination, not asked of the patient.

C.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
C.q: Which term describes lesions that remain separate from one another?
opts: Confluent
Confluent lesions run together, the opposite of lesions that remain separate, which are discrete.
Grouped
Grouped lesions form a cluster; lesions that remain separate from one another are discrete.
Reticular
Reticular describes a lacy or networked pattern; lesions that stay separate from one another are discrete.
Discrete
Correct — discrete lesions stay distinct rather than merging.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
C.q: What is the first step in everting the upper lid to search for a foreign body?
opts: Press on the globe itself to push the lid outward
You never press on the eyeball itself; the patient looks down and the lid is turned over a stick above the tarsal plate.
Use a cotton swab placed at the lid margin itself
The stick goes at least 1 cm above the lid margin, at the upper border of the tarsal plate, after the patient looks down.
Ask the patient to look down and relax
Correct — the patient looks down and relaxes; then the lashes are pulled down and forward over a stick placed 1 cm above the margin.
Ask the patient to look up, then pull the lid upward directly
The patient looks down, not up, and the lashes are pulled gently down and forward rather than straight upward.
C.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 42

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: Which statement about discharge in acute sinusitis is correct?
opts: Discharge is absent in acute sinusitis
Nasal discharge is one of the suggestive features of acute sinusitis, along with local tenderness, pain and fever.
Purulent discharge is suggestive
Correct, and the distinction matters — patients and clinicians both over-read green discharge as proof of bacterial infection. But the COLOR of the discharge is not diagnostic.
Green discharge is diagnostic of bacterial infection
Discharge color is not diagnostic, so green discharge does not prove bacterial infection; purulence is only suggestive.
Clear discharge excludes sinusitis
Clear discharge does not exclude sinusitis, because discharge color is not diagnostic in either direction.

C.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
C.q: Which term describes lesions involving the skin creases and folds?
opts: Palmar-plantar
Palmar-plantar refers to the palms and soles; lesions involving skin creases and folds are intertriginous.
Intertriginous
Correct — the axillae, groin and inframammary folds are the classic intertriginous sites.
Extensor
Extensor distribution involves the outer surfaces of joints, as in psoriasis.
Photodistributed
Photodistributed lesions are confined to sun-exposed skin; lesions in skin creases and folds are intertriginous.

C.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
C.q: What kind of pressure is applied to the bulb during pneumatic otoscopy?
opts: As hard as the patient will tolerate
Force is not what makes the membrane move visibly, and it hurts.
A series of rapid repeated squeezes
Repeated squeezing is not the technique; apply quick, firm but gentle pressure to the bulb and watch the membrane move.
Quick, firm but gentle
Correct. Only a small pressure change is needed; the membrane's movement is slight, and force adds nothing but discomfort.
Slow and sustained, held for several seconds
A sustained squeeze equalizes rather than producing the brief deflection you are watching for.

C.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
C.q: A palpable, elevated, plateau-like solid mass larger than one centimeter that occupies a large area compared with its elevation is called what?
opts: A tumor
A tumor is a solid elevated mass greater than two centimeters, not a broad plateau; that plateau shape is a plaque.
A patch
A patch is flat rather than elevated; a plateau-like, elevated mass over one centimeter is a plaque.
A plaque
Correct — psoriasis is the example, and a plaque may be coalesced papules.
A nodule
A nodule is round or ellipsoid and sits deeper in the dermis rather than being plateau-like.

D.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
D.q: An elevated, circumscribed, encapsulated lesion in the dermis or subcutaneous layer filled with liquid or semisolid material is called what?
opts: A nodule
A nodule is a firm, solid lesion; an encapsulated lesion filled with liquid or semisolid material is a cyst.
A pustule
A pustule is a superficial elevation filled with purulent material; a deeper encapsulated lesion is a cyst.
A cyst
Correct — a cyst is encapsulated and filled with liquid or semisolid material, as in a sebaceous cyst.
A bulla
A bulla is a superficial fluid-filled elevation rather than an encapsulated one.

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
D.q: Which setup is correct for the tuning fork hearing tests?
opts: A 128 hertz fork — the larger one — in a quiet room
The larger low-frequency fork is used to test vibration sense, not hearing.
A 512 hertz fork, with background noise to mask the other ear
A quiet room is specified; masking with noise is not part of the technique.
Any available fork, since only the comparison matters
The frequency is specified, and a low-frequency fork is felt as much as heard.
A 512 hertz fork — the smaller one — in a quiet room
Correct. The frequency matters because it sits in the speech range and rings long enough to compare two positions.

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
D.q: What is the Rinne result in CONDUCTIVE hearing loss?
opts: Bone conduction equal to or greater than air conduction
Correct. Bone conduction equals or outlasts air conduction, because vibrations through bone bypass the impaired external or middle ear to reach the cochlea.
Air conduction greater than bone conduction
That is the normal pattern, which also persists in sensorineural loss.
Neither is heard at all
Conductive loss reduces air conduction; it does not abolish hearing by bone.
Bone conduction is heard but air conduction is heard longer
Air conduction lasting longer is the normal ratio, which also holds in sensorineural loss; conductive loss gives bone equal to or longer than air.

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
D.q: What happens to vision in conjunctivitis?
opts: Vision is normal but the pupil is fixed and mid-dilated
A dilated, fixed pupil belongs to acute glaucoma, where vision is also decreased; conjunctivitis leaves the pupil unaffected.
Vision is decreased and the cornea is steamy
Decreased vision with a steamy cornea is acute glaucoma; conjunctivitis leaves vision unaffected except for mild blurring.
Vision is not affected except for mild blurring from discharge
Correct — conjunctivitis leaves vision unaffected apart from mild blurring from discharge, and the pupil is not affected.
Vision is usually decreased and the pupil is irregular
Decreased vision with a small irregular pupil fits acute iritis; conjunctivitis leaves vision and the pupil unaffected.
D.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 45

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
D.q: When should the lacrimal sac compression test be avoided?
opts: If the patient is over sixty-five
Age is no reason to avoid it; the lacrimal sac compression test is avoided when the area is significantly inflamed or tender.
If the area is significantly inflamed or tender
Correct — the lacrimal sac compression test is avoided if the area is significantly inflamed or tender.
If the patient wears contact lenses
Contact lens wear is no reason to avoid it; the test is avoided only when the area is significantly inflamed or tender.
If the patient has had cataract surgery
Cataract surgery in the elderly is a reason not to dilate the pupils, not to skip this test; avoid it if the area is inflamed.
D.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 38

D.io: g — Documentation of a complete history and physical examination
D.q: What is the rule on abbreviations in written clinical assignments?
opts: Abbreviations are encouraged wherever they shorten the note
Abbreviations are not encouraged; written clinical assignments allow none, so every term is written out in full.
No abbreviations
Correct — written clinical assignments use no abbreviations at all, with no exception for defined or widely known terms.
Abbreviations are acceptable once defined on first use
Defining an abbreviation first does not make it acceptable; written clinical assignments allow no abbreviations at all.
Only widely recognized medical abbreviations may be used
Common medical abbreviations are not exempt; written clinical assignments allow no abbreviations of any kind.
D.cite: Intro to PD II - Elwaya .pdf, Page 20

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
D.q: What additional finding appears in CONGENITAL Horner syndrome?
opts: Bilateral ptosis
Horner ptosis affects the involved side; the congenital form adds a lighter iris on that side, called heterochromia.
Proptosis of the affected eye
Proptosis signals orbital disease; congenital Horner syndrome adds a lighter iris on the affected side.
The involved iris is lighter in color
Correct — in congenital Horner syndrome the involved iris is lighter in color than its fellow, which is called heterochromia.
The involved iris is darker in color
The involved iris is lighter, not darker, than its fellow in congenital Horner syndrome.
D.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 87

D.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
D.q: A circumscribed, flat discoloration measuring less than one centimeter is called what?
opts: A patch
A patch is the same flat discoloration but larger than one centimeter; under one centimeter it is a macule.
A papule
A papule is palpable and elevated rather than flat; a flat discoloration under one centimeter is a macule.
A plaque
A plaque is elevated, plateau-like and over one centimeter; a flat discoloration under one centimeter is a macule.
A macule
Correct — a macule is a circumscribed, flat discoloration under one centimeter, such as a freckle.

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
D.q: Which causes of hoarseness should a history cover?
opts: Viral laryngitis, overuse, reflux, nerve damage, smoking
Correct — a list that runs from the trivial to the serious, which is why hoarseness always earns a full history.
Allergic rhinitis, sinusitis and chronic postnasal drip
Allergic rhinitis, sinusitis and postnasal drip are nasal conditions, not the causes of hoarseness a history covers.
Gingivitis and dental caries
Gingivitis and caries are gum and tooth findings; hoarseness comes from laryngitis, overuse, reflux, nerve damage or smoking.
Presbycusis and tinnitus
Presbycusis and tinnitus are hearing symptoms; hoarseness is a voice symptom with causes such as laryngitis and reflux.

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
D.q: Which cause of red eye shows redness that is DIFFUSE and maximal peripherally, with vision unaffected?
opts: Acute iritis
Acute iritis gives injection of the deeper vessels around the limbus and decreased vision.
Glaucoma
Glaucoma gives deep-vessel redness around the limbus, a steamy cloudy cornea, a dilated fixed pupil and decreased vision.
Corneal injury or infection
Corneal injury or infection gives deep-vessel redness around the limbus with vision usually decreased.
Conjunctivitis
Correct — conjunctivitis gives diffuse conjunctival redness maximal peripherally, with vision affected only by mild blurring.
D.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 48 (image only)

D.io: d — Physical examination findings of abnormal conditions of skin, hair and nails
D.q: A soft tissue infection around the cuticle or nail fold that is painful and purulent is called what?
opts: Nail pitting
Nail pitting is a dystrophy of the nail plate; a painful, purulent infection around the cuticle is acute paronychia.
Acute paronychia
Correct — pain and purulence distinguish the acute form from the chronic one.
Onycholysis
Onycholysis is painless plate separation; a painful, purulent infection of the cuticle or nail fold is acute paronychia.
Subungual hematoma
This is hemorrhage beneath the nail rather than an infection.

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
D.q: A TENDER thyroid suggests what?
opts: A solitary cyst
A cyst presents as a single nodule; tenderness of the gland is the feature that suggests thyroiditis.
Thyroiditis
Correct. Diffuse enlargement splits three ways on texture alone: soft is Graves, firm is Hashimoto, and tender is thyroiditis.
Graves disease
Graves disease makes the gland soft rather than tender; a tender thyroid suggests thyroiditis.
Endemic goiter
Endemic goiter is associated with iodine deficiency; a tender gland suggests thyroiditis instead.

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
D.q: What is the vital sign of the eye?
opts: Intraocular pressure
Intraocular pressure is likened to systemic blood pressure, but visual acuity is the one called the vital sign of the eye.
Pupil reactivity
Pupillary reactions are checked before dilating, but visual acuity is the one called the vital sign of the eye.
Visual fields
Visual field testing follows acuity in the order; visual acuity is the one called the vital sign of the eye.
Visual acuity
Correct — visual acuity testing is called the vital sign of the eye and comes early in the suggested order.
D.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 21

D.io: c — Clinical reasoning in oral presentations
D.q: How should notes be used while presenting a case?
opts: Read from them verbatim so that no detail is omitted
Verbatim reading is exactly what to avoid; the presenter should try not to read from notes while presenting.
Notes are not permitted during a case presentation at all
Notes are not banned outright; the point is to try not to read from them while presenting the case.
Hand the notes to the listener rather than presenting aloud
The presenter delivers the case aloud to the listener; notes stay with the presenter, who tries not to read from them.
Try not to read from them
Correct — reading works directly against helping the listener visualize the patient.
D.cite: Intro to PD II - Elwaya .pdf, Page 9

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
D.q: Which complaints fall in the EMERGENT group, referred to ophthalmology immediately?
opts: Blepharitis, chalazion and dry eye
None of these is on the emergent list, which includes sudden vision loss, chemical burns and globe rupture.
Conjunctivitis and subconjunctival hemorrhage
A subconjunctival hemorrhage is usually harmless, and neither is emergent; chemical burns and rupture are.
Sudden vision loss, retinal artery occlusion, chemical burns, rupture, acute angle-closure glaucoma, and vitreous hemorrhage
Correct — sudden vision loss, retinal artery occlusion, chemical burns, rupture, angle closure and vitreous hemorrhage go to ophthalmology immediately.
Acute glaucoma, orbital cellulitis, corneal ulcer or abrasion, retinal detachment, macular edema, and hyphema
Those are the urgent complaints, sent for ophthalmology follow-up in one day or less rather than immediately.
D.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 124

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
D.q: At what age do conductive and sensorineural hearing loss typically begin?
opts: Both typically begin after sixty
Only sensorineural loss typically begins in middle or later years; conductive loss begins in childhood, up to about age 40.
Both typically begin in childhood
Only conductive loss begins in childhood and young adulthood; sensorineural loss usually begins in middle or later years.
Conductive up to about forty; sensorineural in later years
Correct. Conductive loss usually begins in childhood and young adulthood, up to age 40, and sensorineural loss in middle or later years.
Conductive in middle or later years; sensorineural in childhood
Reversed. Sensorineural loss is the later-onset pattern, and conductive loss is the one that shows up from childhood to about forty.

D.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
D.q: Which term describes grouped papules or vesicles arranged as they are in a herpes simplex infection?
opts: Zosteriform
Zosteriform lesions are clustered in a dermatomal distribution.
Annular
Annular means shaped like a ring; grouped vesicles arranged like herpes simplex are herpetiform.
Confluent
Confluent lesions run together; grouped papules or vesicles arranged like herpes simplex are herpetiform.
Herpetiform
Correct — the configuration is named for the infection it resembles.

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
D.q: A chalky white patch on the tympanic membrane of a patient who once had tympanostomy tubes. Which interpretation is correct?
opts: Tympanosclerosis — usually not significant
Correct. Tympanosclerosis is a hyaline deposit in the membrane after severe otitis media or a healed perforation, and it is usually not clinically significant.
Tympanosclerosis — and it always requires referral
The patch is tympanosclerosis, but it is usually not clinically significant, so it does not always require referral.
A cholesteatoma — and it requires urgent referral
A cholesteatoma is a keratin mass behind or through the membrane, not a flat chalky patch, and it does not follow tube placement.
A healing perforation — which will close spontaneously
The deposit follows severe otitis media or a healed perforation; it is not itself an open perforation.

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
D.q: Besides Sjogren's syndrome, what causes excessive tearing or dryness?
opts: A pterygium growing across the cornea
A pterygium is a triangular conjunctival thickening that may interfere with vision; tearing points to lacrimal obstruction.
Obstruction in the lacrimal apparatus
Correct — excessive tearing or dryness comes from obstruction in the lacrimal apparatus or from Sjogren's syndrome.
Clouding of the lens from a cataract
A cataract is a lens opacity that causes gradual, painless loss of vision, not tearing or dryness.
Raised pressure from simple glaucoma
Simple glaucoma causes gradual, painless visual loss; tearing or dryness points to lacrimal obstruction or Sjogren's syndrome.
D.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 18

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
D.q: Which findings characterize a subconjunctival hemorrhage on examination?
opts: Pain present with photophobia and a hazy cornea
Pain, photophobia and a hazy cornea suggest a corneal injury or ulcer; a subconjunctival hemorrhage is painless with a clear cornea.
Purulent discharge with lid crusting
Purulent discharge suggests bacterial infection; a subconjunctival hemorrhage has no ocular discharge at all.
An irregular pupil with ciliary flush
A small irregular pupil with redness around the limbus fits acute iritis; in a subconjunctival hemorrhage the pupil is unaffected.
Pain absent, vision and pupil unaffected, no discharge, cornea clear
Correct — a subconjunctival hemorrhage is painless with normal vision and pupil, no discharge and a clear cornea.
D.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 44

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
D.q: A headache of SUDDEN, SEVERE onset should raise which diagnosis?
opts: Migraine
Migraine is episodic and typically builds rather than peaking instantly.
Cluster headache
Cluster headache is unilateral; a sudden, severe headache is the pattern that raises subarachnoid hemorrhage.
Subarachnoid hemorrhage
Correct. Sudden and severe is the pattern that cannot be attributed to a benign cause without investigation.
Tension headache
Tension headache is episodic rather than sudden and severe; that onset raises subarachnoid hemorrhage.

D.io: Objective b — Terms describing lesion type (primary morphology), configuration (secondary morphology), texture, distribution and color
D.q: Which term describes twisted, coiled or spiral lesions?
opts: Gyrate
Correct — gyrate describes lesions that are twisted, coiled, spiral or snakelike in shape.
Arciform
Arciform lesions form arcs or curves; twisted, coiled or spiral lesions are described as gyrate.
Reticular
Reticular describes a lacy or networked pattern; twisted, coiled or spiral lesions are gyrate.
Discrete
Discrete lesions remain separate from one another; twisted, coiled or spiral lesions are gyrate.

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
D.q: Which purpose and indication describe the swinging light test?
opts: Alignment of the visual axes; indicated for diplopia
Muscle imbalance is revealed by the cover-uncover test; the swinging light test assesses optic nerve function for anisocoria.
Refractive error; indicated for blurred vision
Refractive error is shown by the pinhole test; the swinging light test assesses optic nerve function and is indicated for anisocoria.
Intraocular pressure; indicated for headache
Pressure is measured with a tonometer pen; the swinging light test assesses optic nerve function and is indicated for anisocoria.
Functional impairment of the optic nerve and the integrity of the visual pathways; indicated for anisocoria
Correct — the swinging light test checks optic nerve function and visual pathway integrity, and its indication is anisocoria.
D.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 74

D.io: d — Physical examination findings of abnormal conditions of skin, hair and nails
D.q: What distinguishes a splinter hemorrhage from a subungual hematoma?
opts: A splinter hemorrhage is painful while a subungual hematoma is painless
Pain does not separate them; a splinter hemorrhage comes from the distal capillary loop, a hematoma bleeds to the nail plate.
A splinter hemorrhage affects all nails while a subungual hematoma affects one
The number of nails does not separate them; the source does: the distal capillary loop versus hemorrhage to the nail plate.
A splinter hemorrhage is a transverse line while a subungual hematoma is longitudinal
Orientation does not separate them; a splinter hemorrhage arises from the distal capillary loop, a hematoma bleeds to the plate.
A splinter hemorrhage arises from the distal capillary loop
Correct — a splinter hemorrhage comes from the distal capillary loop, while a subungual hematoma is hemorrhage to the nail plate.

D.io: e — Clinical skills for a complete and focused skin examination
D.q: Which equipment should be available for a skin examination?
opts: A ruler and a light source only
A ruler and a light source are not enough; a magnifying lens and gloves for any open lesions are also needed.
A dermatoscope and a Wood's lamp
Neither instrument is part of the kit; the equipment for a skin examination is a ruler, a light source, a magnifying lens and gloves.
A tape measure and a skin marking pen
A tape measure and marking pen are not the kit; the equipment is a ruler, a light source, a magnifying lens and gloves.
A ruler, a light source, a magnifying lens
Correct — gloves for any open lesions complete the kit, and the ruler matters because many lesion definitions turn on one centimeter.

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
D.q: A temporal field defect in one eye should prompt what?
opts: Testing for a nasal defect in the other eye
Correct — a temporal defect in one eye may suggest a nasal defect in the other eye, so test that possibility.
Immediate fundoscopy of the same eye only
Fundoscopy is not the next step; a temporal defect in one eye may mean a nasal defect in the other, which should be tested.
Repeating acuity in the same eye
Acuity is not the next step; a temporal field defect in one eye should prompt testing the other eye for a nasal defect.
Measuring intraocular pressure
Pressure is not the next step; a temporal field defect in one eye should prompt testing the other eye for a nasal defect.
D.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 55

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced Ocular Medical History and Examination
D.q: How is a corneal scar distinguished from a cataract on examination?
opts: The scar is painful; the cataract is not
Pain does not separate them; the scar is a superficial corneal opacity and the cataract lies deeper, behind the pupil.
The scar affects vision more than the cataract
Effect on vision is not the test; the scar is a superficial corneal opacity and the cataract lies deeper, behind the pupil.
The scar is a superficial grayish-white corneal opacity
Correct — a corneal scar is a superficial grayish white opacity, while a cataract lies deeper and is seen only through the pupil.
The scar is visible only through the pupil; the cataract is superficial
This reverses them: the scar is superficial in the cornea, and the cataract is on a deeper plane, seen through the pupil.
D.cite: PD II Advanced Exam Ocular Lecture - Beck.pptx, Slide 92

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
D.q: What is a NORMAL Rinne result?
opts: Both heard for exactly the same duration
Equal duration is grouped with the conductive finding, not the normal one.
Neither heard, in a quiet room
A normal patient hears both, and hears the tone longer through air than through bone.
Air conduction heard longer than bone conduction
Correct. Normally sound is heard longer through air than through bone, so air conduction outlasts bone conduction.
Bone conduction heard longer than air conduction
Bone conduction outlasting air conduction is the conductive hearing loss result, not the normal one.

D.io: Instructional Objectives — Advanced ENT History and Examination
D.q: Which scalp and skin conditions are looked for during the head examination?
opts: Only nevi and keratoses
Nevi and keratoses are only part of it; lice, seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis are also looked for.
Lice, seborrheic dermatitis, psoriasis, atypical nevi and actinic keratosis
Correct. The scalp is easy to skip and carries both infestation and premalignant change.
Only alopecia and scarring
Hair loss and scars are looked for, but so are lice, seborrheic dermatitis, psoriasis, atypical nevi and actinic keratosis.
Only lice
Lice are looked for, but so are seborrheic dermatitis, psoriasis, atypical nevi and actinic keratosis.

D.io: e — Clinical skills for a complete and focused skin examination
D.q: Which characteristics of the skin are assessed by inspection, palpation or both?
opts: Color and lesions only, since the skin examination is essentially visual
Moisture, temperature, texture, mobility and turgor all require palpation.
Temperature and turgor only, since color varies too much between patients
